questions.q: A 75-year-old male is noticing decreased muscle strength and function, making it difficult to rise from a chair. This condition, characterized by the age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass and strength, is known as:
questions.explain: Sarcopenia is defined as the age-related loss of muscle mass, strength, and function.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Nutrition Through the Life Span
questions.subject: HOSA Nutrition

questions.q: To prevent sarcopenia, recent research suggests that older adults may need higher protein intake than the standard RDA. What is the recommended range often cited for this population?
questions.explain: Standard RDA is 0.8 g/kg, but for the elderly, expert groups recommend 1.0-1.2 g/kg/day to maintain muscle mass and combat anabolic resistance.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Nutrition Through the Life Span
questions.subject: HOSA Nutrition

questions.q: Why are older adults at a higher risk for Vitamin B12 deficiency despite adequate dietary intake?
options: Increased excretion of B12 by the kidneys
Atrophic gastritis reducing stomach acid and Intrinsic Factor production
Excessive consumption of fiber binding the vitamin
questions.explain: Atrophic gastritis affects many older adults, reducing HCl and Intrinsic Factor secretion, both of which are necessary for separating B12 from protein and absorbing it in the ileum.

questions.q: Which factor most significantly contributes to the increased risk of dehydration in the elderly?
options: Increased efficiency of kidneys to concentrate urine
questions.explain: The thirst sensation diminishes with age. Elderly individuals often do not feel thirsty even when dehydrated.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Nutrition Through the Life Span
questions.subject: HOSA Nutrition

questions.q: Vitamin D deficiency is common in the elderly due to which of the following factors?
options: Increased conversion of Vitamin D in the skin
Reduced capacity of the skin to synthesize Vitamin D and less sun exposure
Higher absorption rates in the intestine
Increased conversion to the active form by the kidneys
questions.explain: Aging skin synthesizes Vitamin D less efficiently (approx. 50% less capacity by age 70), and kidneys are less efficient at converting it to the active hormone.

questions.q: An 80-year-old patient has dysphagia following a stroke. Which dietary modification is most appropriate to prevent aspiration?
options: Thickened liquids and pureed or soft-textured foods
questions.explain: Dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) requires modifying texture to ensure safety. Thickened liquids move slower, allowing more control, and soft foods reduce choking risk.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Nutrition Through the Life Span
questions.subject: HOSA Nutrition

questions.q: Social isolation in the elderly often leads to poor nutritional intake. Which community-based program specifically addresses this by delivering prepared meals to homebound seniors?
questions.explain: Meals on Wheels is a well-known program that provides home-delivered meals to seniors who are unable to shop or cook, addressing both nutrition and isolation.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Nutrition Through the Life Span

questions.q: Xerostomia is a common condition in the elderly, often caused by medications. How does it impact nutritional status?
options: It causes difficulty chewing and swallowing due to dry mouth
questions.explain: Xerostomia (dry mouth) reduces saliva, which is needed for lubricating food (bolus formation) and initial digestion, making eating difficult and reducing intake.
